item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 17 November 2026
item.description:
Tipa opens with AI gripes, then gets to the good stuff: a lightly attended Malifaux tournament and Rasputina squaring off against Sandeep Desai.

UltrViolet rounds up November gaming with Modern Warfare 4, Ravenfield, WoW: Forever, zombie hordes, and GTA VI looming over the SSD.

Sey unexpectedly falls for Milki Delivery, a cozy bike-courier game where cute vibes and Milki’s milk runs make resource gathering click.

Azuriel roasts the absurdity of GTA6 snagging Game Awards nominations, including Best Performance, before the game is even out.

Ellie recommends Botany Manor as a short, calming puzzle game about coaxing rare plants to bloom by piecing together scattered horticultural clues.

Wilhelm’s Stardew Valley farm life hits new milestones: horse stables, Willy’s boat repairs, and the wizard’s ex-wife sending them swampward.

Andrew Plotkin is pausing Visible Zorker’s regular cadence in December to compare three Zork 1 source versions, bug fixes and all.

Heartless keeps it simple and delighted: the Vikings crushed the Packers 30-10, and Thanksgiving suddenly looks sweeter.

Joar argues the activities that stick are the ones with a built-in next date and a little commitment, from OLLI to dance classes.

Mike digs into a weird Apple II clone with flimsy plastics, a loose speaker, and a probably bootleg ASCII-branded 65C02.

Axxuy realizes the bus ride to visit their partner is perfect for offline blogging, touch-typing, and making the commute feel pleasantly shorter.

Patrick finds E.R. Eddison’s Mistress of Mistresses gloriously strange: pagan prayer, portal fantasy, dynastic drama, and intense masculine relationships all at once.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 16 November 2026
item.description:
Cliffski readies Ridiculous Space Battles for early access, framing it as a fun solo passion project with firm pricing and zero patience for entitlement.

Frostilyte heads into Pokémon Silver’s League finale with an E-tier team, lots of prep, and real anxiety about Will’s Psychic-heavy opener.

Joel recommends Strange Jigsaws as a clever, spoiler-sensitive puzzle box that twists classic jigsaw ideas across screens, UI, and even the pause menu.

Kimimi finds Vampire Night atmospheric and mechanically sharp, even if its voice acting and tagalong child seriously test the gothic mood.

Margot’s week mixes Doom running on an oscilloscope and CSS, retro handheld setup with the Retroid Pocket Duo, and finishing Minishoot’ Adventures.

Wilhelm tracks Fantasy Critic swings as Warhammer Survivors bumps rankings, with GTA6 looming and his World of Warcraft: Forever pick posting an 82.

The Chronicler comes away impressed by Dust in the Wind, a PHALANX prototype mixing western campaign storytelling, resource pressure, and tactical combat.

CrazyKinux thinks Blade Runner 2099’s final trailer nails the atmosphere, while hoping the series leaves enough quiet space to really breathe.

Tofutush tackles place-based prompts through Shenzhen with funny guesswork, local water and plants, and plenty of side-eye for Anglocentric assumptions.

Juhis shares a strong Djangonaut week: bug-fixing RSVP status, planning an audit log, and enjoying the Django community’s collaborative conference prep.

Wes uses Ocarina of Time, UltraHLE, and AI-assisted emulation to argue Nintendo-style platform control is breaking down fast.

Roger says Blaugust 2026 revived his writing rhythm, and the payoff looks real with stronger traffic, better contacts, and a growing niche audience.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 15 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae battles through Divinity: Original Sin 2’s Wrecker’s Cove, regrouping a split party amid Voidwoken, cursed choke points, and heaps of corpses.

Krista spotlights Tricky Madness as an SSX-inspired arcade snowboarder built for absurd speed, huge tricks, and wild lines through Early Access courses.

Luna wraps Spooktober with Gloomy Eyes frustrations, Rhythm Paradise Groove family fun, crochet plans, and finally taking the plunge on a Steam Machine.

Wilhelm charts 689 Amarr systems in EVE Online for Blessed Pilgrim, juggling Crimson Harvest sites and DOTLAN map markups along the way.

Bhagpuss spins a delightfully rambling music roundup, hopping from Carottes to 1000 Rabbits while chasing a half-remembered French classroom song.

Ramen Junkie mixes toy-store malaise with bargain finds, mulling Ross overflow and celebrating $5 Blokees like Optimus Prime, Bumblebee, and Jeff the Land Shark.

Cristian reflects on Romania’s Christmas fast, fish-permitted days, and the yearly clash between slowing down spiritually and the holiday shopping rush.

Jeff argues outages show why ops teams need stubborn friction, especially around logging, resilience, and the risky temptation to debug in production.

Warner likes the iPad mini 8 for keeping the same useful form while adding OLED, Wi‑Fi 7, better durability, and a landscape Center Stage camera.

Bruce Schneier posts a quick speaking schedule update with stops at Catalyst Summit in Brampton and QT Qonference 2026 in Toronto.

Dave Winer says BonBon’s nearly out, pitches a Markdown-based new web, and vents about how the tech industry fumbled the web we had.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 14 November 2026
item.description:
Krista mixes fresh impressions of the Nintendo Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake with a warm look back at her history with Hyrule.

Margot recommends Minishoot’ Adventures as a charming twin-stick shooter-metroidvania hybrid where exploration, secrets, and steady upgrades really carry the day.

Shintar is happily ignoring WoW Forever optimization pressure, rolling alts across starter zones, and enjoying a more horizontal first week.

Marc revisits WiiWare’s awkward history and shines a light on Orbient, one of Skip Ltd.’s polished Art Style puzzle releases.

Wilhelm rounds up expansion news, from Guild Wars Afterlife’s roguelike dungeon runs to EverQuest Legends’ Rulers of Kunark and its revamped Kunark politics.

The Chronicler spotlights The Weimar Republic, a GMT card-driven COIN-style game about Germany’s 1919–1933 power struggle with strong solo support.

Anarchae makes a practical case for symptom tracking: not for optimization, but for giving doctors clearer timelines on meds, side effects, and chronic issues.

Roger reflects on filling a blank office wall with paintings, family art, and a Peter Cushing autograph, turning decor into personal storytelling.

Tobold argues Nvidia’s slide exposed a scary concentration risk: too much market value and too much company power tied to Jensen Huang.

Kelly uses the Microsoft outage to argue that cloud centralization around Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace has made corporate tech far less resilient.

JJM laments how AI crawler defenses are making GitHub, GitLab, SourceHut, and even IMDb more annoying for anyone browsing logged out.

Jimmy points readers to a new Analog Antiquarian piece on Titus Andronicus, more quick dispatch than full post.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 13 November 2026
item.description:
Sey rounds up indie picks like MONOMOON, Flexible Frosty, and Pelikeeper, then shares excitement for Milki Delivery and finally digging into Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

Bhagpuss revisits Cyberpunk: Edgerunners with a soundtrack-first lens, arguing season two is good but can’t quite match season one’s iconic punch.

Kimimi makes a lovely case for Kirby’s Adventure as pure play, where Kirby’s charm, copy abilities, and tiny bits of whimsy make every action delightful.

Ramen Junkie finds the Sky: Children of the Light Nendoroid a solid, affordable Moth-era Sky Kid figure, even if customization fans may want more flair.

Mailvaltar says getting ganked in ArcheAge unexpectedly rekindled his interest, especially by pushing him to finally think harder about rifles and Gunslinger.

Scopique breaks down Squadron 42’s new footage, from the hospital aftermath and character creator to life aboard the UEES Stanton.

Wilhelm recaps EVE Online’s move back from Siseide, with capital jump logistics, timer bashes, and a huge Amamake slugfest melting trillions in nullsec toys.

Juhis walks through modernizing a Django Girls admin tool with vanilla JavaScript, then adding an audit log to track RSVP and application changes.

Warner is baffled that Apple’s iOS 27 spam-call cleanup sometimes works in one tap, sometimes needs three, and never feels actually fixed.

Bruce Schneier argues AI doesn’t need to go rogue to cause chaos; it just has to get really good at hacking social, political, and software systems.

Dave Winer cheers Claude for resurfacing an old Fargo demo site from fuzzy memories, then pivots to the perennial question of what tech billionaires do with all that money.

Cristian posts a quick Gentoo-on-PowerPC meme shot—more tiny tech ephemera than essay, but fun if that niche hits for you.
